clue.text: Leave out John's fish

parts.note: to leave something out is to skip it
Jack is a familiar form of the name John; the 's is just a link

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop some fish belonging to a man called John.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipjack is a kind of tuna, a striped ocean fish.

clue.text: Record run

definitions.meaning: a short music release on one disc
in cricket a ... is one run

explanation.surface: Two terse words that might be a sports headline about a fastest time.
explanation.definitionFit: A single is a short record and also a cricket score of one run.

clue.text: Turn up in green

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: Someone arrives dressed in green.
explanation.definitionFit: To invert is to turn upside down, here read as turn up.

clue.text: Post was placed between two articles in American dish

parts.note: a jamb is the upright post of a door or window frame

indicators.note: between says the placing part sits inside the pair of articles

parts.note: A is an indefinite article, taken twice
lay is the past tense of lie, to be placed

explanation.surface: A letter was positioned between two newspaper pieces about a US recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests mail, but it is a door post. 'between' puts LAY inside A and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Louisiana rice dish with meat and seafood.

clue.text: From sofa, encourage those running round street

indicators.note: round says the encouraging word goes about the street

parts.note: to encourage is to cheer
the runners in a race are collectively the field

explanation.surface: Spectators rise from the sofa to cheer runners going round a street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is only a link; 'round' looks as if it goes with the runners but wraps the street in the encouraging word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a padded leather couch with buttoned back and arms.

clue.text: Advise one's playing well

definitions.meaning: to advise someone is to tell them facts, a verb
a player on good form is said to be ..., as a two-word phrase

explanation.surface: Someone gives advice about a player who is performing well.
explanation.definitionFit: To advise is to give notice or tell, a straight synonym; read as two words it describes a player at their best.

clue.text: One dangling on end of hangman's rope

definitions.text: One dangling on end of hangman's rope

parts.words: One dangling on end of hangman's rope
parts.note: the loop tied at the end of the executioner's rope, which hangs down from the gallows

explanation.surface: A grim picture of something swinging from a gallows rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The running loop at the end of a hangman's rope is the thing that dangles from it.

clue.text: In vacation, worked out a Strauss role

indicators.note: letters that are worked out are reorganised into a fresh order

explanation.surface: While on holiday, someone practised a part from a Strauss opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges VACATION. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavian is the young nobleman in Richard Strauss's opera Der Rosenkavalier.

clue.text: More than half of French captured, without boasting

indicators.note: captured says one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: mostly means for the most part, more than half
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Over half the French were taken prisoner, and nobody bragged about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' reads as soldiers taken prisoner, but it signals the French word sitting inside the English one.
explanation.definitionFit: To act modestly is to behave without bragging, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Some weeks, mob never riots

indicators.note: riots are wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: For several weeks a mob has never rioted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riots' rearranges the letters of MOB NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh month lasts a little over four weeks, so it is a span of some weeks.

clue.text: Sort of history of some shrimps?

definitions.meaning: a short, condensed account is called a ... history
shrimps preserved in butter in a pot are a classic British dish

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of history some shrimps might have.
explanation.walkthrough: Potted shrimps are brown shrimps sealed in spiced butter, a traditional dish from Morecambe Bay in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A potted history is an abridged one; potted shrimps are preserved in a pot.

clue.text: Emma, a novel title

parts.note: the heroine named Emma whose married name gives the title of a Flaubert novel, with a French title of address

explanation.surface: Emma is the name of a famous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma suggests Jane Austen, but the Emma meant is Flaubert's heroine, Emma Bovary.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's novel is named for its heroine Emma, whose title is the French one for a married woman.

clue.text: Abandoned a girl

parts.note: lorn is an old poetic word for forsaken or abandoned

explanation.surface: Someone has deserted a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna is a girl's name, as in the novel Lorna Doone.

clue.text: Thieves duck, approaching part of roof

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck
the eaves are the overhanging lower edge of a roof

explanation.surface: Burglars dodge down as they near a section of rooftop.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'tea leaves' means thieves, because the two rhyme. The stray mark in the held clue is a speck on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: the phrase rhymes with and stands for crooks who steal.

clue.text: Solid defence, but in all wars had to struggle

indicators.note: to struggle is to thrash about, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sturdy fortification, yet amid all wars it had a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to struggle' rearranges IN ALL WARS HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman wall across northern England was built as a fortified frontier barrier.

clue.text: Simple comic act hit by criticism

parts.note: to hit is to slap
stick is informal British for criticism, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: A basic comedy routine is panned by critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is broad physical comedy, the simplest kind of comic routine.

clue.text: Squirrel's lunchtime —- tucked into hearty portion

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: tucked into says the time goes inside the portion

parts.note: a chunk is a big piece
1 pm is lunchtime, written with I for one

explanation.surface: A squirrel tucks into a large helping at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like the squirrel eating, but it signals the time going inside the portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipmunk is a small striped North American ground squirrel.

clue.text: Accidentally discover what's said to be nearer me

indicators.note: what's said signals that a phrase is spoken and heard

parts.note: nearer to the speaker is over here

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a remark meant to bring them closer.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhear is to catch someone's words by chance, finding out unintentionally.

clue.text: Like a lolly, Sir Robin? Enjoy yourself!

parts.note: to fancy an ice lolly is to want to have an ice
Sir Robin Day was a famous British television political interviewer

explanation.surface: Someone asks a famous knight if he would like an ice lolly, then wishes him well.
explanation.walkthrough: An ice lolly is the British name for a frozen treat on a stick, an ice; Sir Robin Day was a leading BBC current-affairs presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A common parting wish meaning have a good time, used as an exclamation.

clue.text: Sort of rice I covered in film

indicators.note: covered says the rice wraps around the letter

parts.note: Patna is a long-grain rice from India

explanation.surface: A grain of rice is coated in a thin layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' puts I inside PATNA; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin surface film, as on old bronze.

clue.text: Group of organisms not entirely widespread

definitions.note: the answer is plural, a group of such categories, while the definition is singular

indicators.note: not entirely says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: general means widespread

explanation.surface: A biological group that is not quite universal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the last letter of GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are the taxonomic ranks grouping species of organisms.

clue.text: See fine miscellany, after opening artist's sample work

indicators.note: fine and miscellany are placed after the opening

parts.note: a port is an opening, as in a porthole
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an olio is a mixture or miscellany

explanation.surface: Look over a fine assortment of work after the gallery's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is an introductory link, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's portfolio is a case or collection of samples of their work.

clue.text: Tragic figure, the opposite of obese in America

indicators.note: the opposite of says swap what is inside what
in signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: obese means fat

explanation.surface: A doomed character is the reverse of an overweight American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obese in America' read literally would put the country inside the fat word; 'the opposite of' reverses which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: Goethe's Faust, who sells his soul to the devil, is a tragic hero.

clue.text: Cutting blade to hand pieces out

definitions.meaning: the cutting blade of a plough is called a ploughshare
to divide something into portions and give them out

explanation.surface: Someone uses a sharp blade to cut and hand out portions.
explanation.definitionFit: A plough's blade is its share; to share is to apportion among people.

clue.text: Finished going to London, after being taken advantage of

indicators.note: the going-to-London part comes after the advantage part

parts.note: someone exploited has been used
travelling to the capital is traditionally called going up to London

explanation.surface: A tired traveller, done in after heading to London and being exploited.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go 'up' to London from anywhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up means exhausted or finished, with nothing left.

clue.text: Discharge one ancient warship, back from the sea

indicators.note: back says the whole string of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: to discharge is to emit
the Roman numeral for one is I
a ram was a warship with an armoured beak

explanation.surface: An old warship fires a single shot and returns from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EMITIRAM round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes things relating to or coming from the sea.

clue.text: Deserve top honours upfront in fighting system

indicators.note: the honours go in front of the deserving part

parts.note: in card games the king and ace are top honours
to deserve something is to rate it

explanation.surface: A fighter earns top awards early in a martial arts contest.
explanation.walkthrough: K and A are the card abbreviations for king and ace, the highest honours in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese unarmed combat method, a fighting discipline.

clue.text: In school hall, foreign dignitary attends a sports competition

parts.note: a gym is a school's hall for exercise
a khan is a ruler or official in central Asia

explanation.surface: An eastern potentate turns up at a sports event in a school hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymkhana is a meeting with horse-riding contests and races.
